nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter, then uses it in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.

A message filter that assigns messages to different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of a user action.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into various folders for a user and stores first classification data in a persistent store.
A model generated by the multi-pass message filter during the first pass, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location and purged after use.

An analysis pass that scans messages in a user's mail folders, reads sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, message contents, and attachments, and trains the multi-pass message filter.
A pass that uses the generated classification model to retrospectively inspect and score messages, generating a misclassification identification of sorted messages.
A list of sorted messages identified as potentially misclassified, displayed to the user so misclassified messages can be moved to a different folder.

A device configured to receive messages, assign them to different message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over the network to the message folders.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform the multi-pass message filtering actions.

A device that executes the multi-pass message filter, generates and stores second classification data in non-persistent memory, scores messages, identifies incorrectly sorted messages, and provides a display of information enabling a user to move messages.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.
A memory-resident-only storage location where the generated classification model resides, not stored on disk or another persistent data store, and from which it is purged.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.
A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.
A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and inspected by the multi-pass message filter.
Email messages received, sorted into folders, and analyzed by the filters.

A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder, who may select the multi-pass message filter for execution through an interface on the client device.<SEP>A person whose mail folders are scanned and who is presented a list of potentially misclassified messages to move to different folders.

A book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address therein may be analyzed to generate second classification data.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that may be analyzed to determine whether a message sender's address is present.
A header of a message, including a subject, analyzed during classification model generation.
The contents of a message analyzed during classification model generation.
Attachments within messages read during the first pass.
Information about the sender of a message read during the first pass.
The network address from which a message originates, read during the first pass.

An interface on the client device through which a user may select the multi-pass message filter for execution.<SEP>An interface on the client device through which a user can select the multi-pass message filter for execution.

A message filter executed in multiple passes on sorted messages; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message and identify messages sorted into incorrect message folders.
Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.

Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train it; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device and is deleted upon providing the display of information.
A folder to which messages are assigned; a message may be identified as stored into an incorrect message folder and moved to another message folder.
A communication item received in plurality, assigned to message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially identified as sorted into an incorrect folder.
A communications network over which messages are communicated between the network device and the client device.
A memory store at the client device where second classification data resides exclusively.
